coverage.selection: 63 individually reviewed primary publications: the original 22 retained unchanged, plus 41 earlier publications selected for decade context. This is a reading selection, not an exhaustive incident database.
coverage.date_policy: All curated entries use actual supported publication dates for their window and chronology. Exact supported event days remain separate; null event dates do not assert an incident's start. Later page updates are described without replacing original publication dates.
limitations: At least one selected publication falls in every calendar year touched by the decade window; many months and some quarters have no selected publication. Absence never means absence of incidents.
Counts describe publications, not unique attacks, victims, campaigns or vulnerabilities. Different first-party reports can concern related activity.
The 2016 and 2026 boundary years are partial. The earliest selected publication is 2016-11-01, not the window's 2016-10-24 start.
Some disclosures describe attacks from earlier months or years. The incident day, detection day, initial disclosure, subsequent updates and retrieval date are distinct.
Known/reported/unknown describe evidence in the cited material reviewed at curation time. Unknown is not a current safety verdict; historical patch instructions can be superseded.
The selected CrowdStrike 2024 postmortem concerns a defective update and availability failure, not a documented malicious intrusion.
Current publisher pages can contain corrections or later findings; dates are supported by explicit original publication statements or dated advisory histories.
The separate CISA KEV collection uses catalog-addition dates, not original disclosure, first exploitation or a personal remediation deadline.
This selection does not establish exposure or compromise of the reader's devices and does not authorize scanning or remediation.

entries.title: Microsoft details STRONTIUM Flash and Windows zero-day attacks
entries.summary: Microsoft describes a targeted spear-phishing campaign chaining an Adobe Flash flaw with Windows kernel privilege escalation. The report illustrates browser-to-kernel trust boundaries and distinguishes observed attacks from the planned Windows patch release.

entries.title: Cloudflare explains its parser memory-leak incident
entries.summary: Cloudflare reports that an HTML parser bug exposed memory containing cookies, tokens and other request data, with some leaks cached by search engines. This was an information-disclosure defect; the report does not establish malicious exploitation of every leaked secret.

entries.title: Microsoft analyzes WannaCry's SMB-based ransomware spread
entries.summary: Microsoft documents WannaCry using a previously patched SMB vulnerability to spread between vulnerable Windows systems. The account highlights patch deployment and legacy-protocol risk; the observed outbreak date and the earlier MS17-010 patch date are separate.

entries.title: Microsoft traces the Petya outbreak through updates and lateral movement
entries.summary: Microsoft's evolving account of the outbreak commonly called NotPetya links some initial infections to the legitimate MEDoc updater and explains credential-assisted lateral movement. Treat the June report as dated research, with its linked follow-up and later corrections.

entries.title: Cisco Talos finds a malicious payload in signed CCleaner releases
entries.summary: Talos identifies malware in a CCleaner installer distributed through legitimate infrastructure and carrying a valid publisher signature. The case shows why signing alone cannot establish that a release is benign; affected release windows differ from the September disclosure.

entries.title: Project Zero publishes speculative-execution memory-disclosure research
entries.summary: Project Zero describes three speculative-execution side channels associated with Spectre and Meltdown and demonstrates impacts across selected security boundaries. Research proofs of concept do not establish real-world compromise of every affected processor or deployment.

entries.title: GitHub reports a memcached-amplification DDoS outage
entries.summary: GitHub describes a February 28 availability attack amplified through publicly exposed memcached servers and its traffic-mitigation response. The report separates service disruption from confidentiality or integrity loss; the March publication is not the attack date.

entries.title: Drupal discloses unauthenticated remote code execution in core
entries.summary: Drupal's advisory describes CVE-2018-7600 across multiple Drupal 7 and 8 subsystems and lists affected ranges and fixed releases. This disclosure is historical guidance; the selected page alone is not a current compromise assessment or a complete later exploitation timeline.

entries.title: Facebook discloses access-token theft through View As bugs
entries.summary: Facebook reports that interacting View As and video-upload bugs let attackers obtain account access tokens. Its initial investigation, subsequent updates and token revocation illustrate how session credentials can remain a security boundary beyond passwords.

entries.title: Kubernetes explains the runc container-escape vulnerability
entries.summary: The Kubernetes security committee explains CVE-2019-5736 in the underlying runc container runtime, including host-root consequences and configuration-dependent mitigations. Container deployment alone is not an isolation guarantee; review the exact runtime and historical advisory scope.

entries.title: Drupal warns of code execution through web-service field handling
entries.summary: Drupal discloses CVE-2019-6340 in field handling for certain web-service configurations. Its February 22 update reports known exploitation and clarifies that enabled REST resources accepting GET can also be affected; the publication and update dates remain distinct.

entries.title: Kaspersky details the ASUS Live Update supply-chain attack
entries.summary: Kaspersky describes malicious ASUS Live Update software found during its investigation. The report dates the attack to June–November 2018, despite its March 2019 disclosure, and highlights the risk of targeted payloads delivered through a trusted update channel.

entries.title: Microsoft releases BlueKeep Remote Desktop Services guidance
entries.summary: Microsoft discloses CVE-2019-0708 in Remote Desktop Services on selected older Windows versions and warns of wormable potential. The initial notice says exploitation had not been observed then; that historical statement is not a claim about subsequent attacks or current safety.

entries.title: Check Point discloses SIGRed in Windows DNS Server
entries.summary: Check Point describes CVE-2020-1350, a Windows DNS Server flaw triggered by crafted DNS responses with potential privileged code execution. Its demonstration and wormability assessment do not prove an operational campaign; affected server roles and versions matter.

entries.title: Twitter explains employee phishing behind account takeovers
entries.summary: Twitter's July 18 account, updated July 30, describes a July 15 phone spear-phishing attack that led to employee credentials and internal support-tool access. The case highlights privileged support workflows, account segmentation and response evidence beyond password resets.

entries.title: CERT-EU tracks Zerologon domain-controller risk and exploitation
entries.summary: CERT-EU explains CVE-2020-1472 in Netlogon authentication and the risk of domain compromise from a network foothold. Its September 25 update incorporates Microsoft-reported attacks; the September 15 initial publication is not the exploitation start date.

entries.title: FireEye reveals SUNBURST in SolarWinds Orion updates
entries.summary: FireEye reports a global intrusion campaign delivered through trojanized SolarWinds Orion updates and publishes detection material. The account illustrates post-compromise identity and network investigation; later attribution updates should not be mistaken for the original disclosure date.

entries.title: Microsoft reports Exchange zero-day exploitation
entries.summary: Microsoft reports an on-premises Exchange exploit chain used to access mail and install persistence. Later updates describe attacks beyond the initially tracked HAFNIUM cluster. Exchange Online is outside the original affected-product scope; patching and compromise investigation are separate tasks.

entries.title: Codecov discloses its Bash Uploader credential-exfiltration incident
entries.summary: Codecov reports unauthorized changes to its Bash Uploader that exfiltrated CI environment variables and repository information. The affected period preceded the April 15 notice. The incident demonstrates how build-tool compromise can expose credentials beyond the code being built.

entries.title: FBI confirms DarkSide ransomware in Colonial Pipeline compromise
entries.summary: The FBI confirms that DarkSide ransomware was responsible for the Colonial Pipeline network compromise. This brief statement establishes the agency's confirmation; it does not provide a full intrusion timeline, initial-access explanation or proof of direct operational-technology compromise.

entries.title: Microsoft tracks NOBELIUM abuse of a legitimate mailing service
entries.summary: Microsoft describes NOBELIUM's use of Constant Contact resources to distribute malicious links while impersonating a development organization. The May 25 escalation followed earlier campaign activity. Trusted email infrastructure and authentic-looking senders do not establish safe content.

entries.title: CERT-EU issues Log4Shell guidance and tracks later Log4j flaws
entries.summary: CERT-EU describes CVE-2021-44228 in Log4j and reports of active exploitation, then records subsequent related flaws and revised mitigations. The evolving advisory illustrates why a first patch or version recommendation may be superseded; consult current supported guidance.

entries.title: Okta concludes its January support-vendor compromise investigation
entries.summary: Okta's concluding report narrows the January support-vendor incident to a brief period of attacker control and limited tenant access, superseding broader early potential-impact estimates. The April publication is a follow-up investigation, not the date of the January compromise.

entries.title: Twilio discloses employee phishing and customer-data access
entries.summary: Twilio reports employee-targeted text-message phishing that yielded credentials and access to some customer data. The archived page explicitly identifies August 7 as its initial publication and includes later October findings; the current page header is not substituted for that original date.

entries.title: Cloudflare explains how security keys blocked a phishing intrusion
entries.summary: Cloudflare describes a July 20 employee phishing attempt resembling attacks on other companies. Some employees entered credentials, but required physical security keys prevented access. This is a documented blocked attempt, not a claim that Cloudflare suffered the same breach as Twilio.

entries.title: Uber describes contractor-account compromise and internal access
entries.summary: Uber's September 16 notice, expanded September 19, describes a compromised contractor account, repeated authentication prompts and access to internal tools. The report underscores the need to scope privileged sessions and downstream credentials; the initial notice and later findings are distinct.

entries.title: Mandiant links 3CX compromise to an earlier poisoned software package
entries.summary: Mandiant's incident-response investigation links the 3CX Desktop App supply-chain compromise to malicious software obtained from Trading Technologies. The case demonstrates one software supply-chain intrusion enabling another; the April report follows the March discovery and response.

entries.title: Singapore CSA warns of active MOVEit Transfer exploitation
entries.summary: CSA warns that CVE-2023-34362 in MOVEit Transfer is reportedly being exploited, with potential unauthorized access, code execution and data theft. Its advisory and later updates concern specific product versions; a file-transfer deployment alone does not establish compromise.

entries.title: Microsoft discloses forged-token access to cloud email
entries.summary: Microsoft reports Storm-0558 access to customer cloud email using forged authentication tokens and an acquired consumer signing key. The account highlights token-validation boundaries between consumer and enterprise systems and links a later technical investigation.

entries.title: Okta reports unauthorized access to support-case files
entries.summary: Okta reports stolen-credential access to its support case-management system and customer-uploaded files. It explains that HAR diagnostic files can contain session tokens. Support-system exposure must be distinguished from the production identity service and from the separate January 2022 incident.

entries.title: Mandiant investigates Citrix Bleed session hijacking
entries.summary: Mandiant documents CVE-2023-4966 exploitation against NetScaler ADC and Gateway, enabling takeover of legitimate sessions despite password and MFA controls. The October 31 investigation dates observed zero-day activity to late August; publication does not establish the campaign's start.

entries.title: Volexity identifies an Ivanti VPN zero-day exploit chain
entries.summary: Volexity reports authentication bypass and command injection chained against Ivanti Connect Secure, followed by credential theft and modified appliance components. Its December 2023 investigation preceded this January disclosure; applying mitigation alone does not remove an existing compromise.

entries.title: US and UK authorities announce LockBit infrastructure disruption
entries.summary: Authorities describe seizing infrastructure and disrupting the LockBit ransomware operation with international partners. This is a dated law-enforcement action, not proof that all affiliates, copies of the malware or future ransomware activity were permanently eliminated.

entries.title: Red Hat warns of malicious code in XZ Utils release packages
entries.summary: Red Hat describes CVE-2024-3094 and malicious code in XZ 5.6.0/5.6.1, including differences between release packages and Git source. Distribution and build details affect applicability; detecting a backdoor is not proof that every affected installation was remotely exploited.

entries.title: Mandiant tracks stolen credentials targeting Snowflake customer instances
entries.summary: Mandiant reports UNC5537 data theft and extortion using stolen customer credentials against Snowflake instances, including accounts without MFA. The investigation concerns customer identity and configuration exposure; it does not establish a breach of Snowflake's underlying platform.

entries.title: CrowdStrike publishes its preliminary Windows outage review
entries.summary: CrowdStrike explains how defective Rapid Response Content caused Windows crashes on July 19. This was an update-validation and availability incident, not a documented malicious intrusion. The preliminary July 24 report is distinct from the event and the later full root-cause analysis.

entries.title: Chainalysis traces the February Bybit cryptocurrency theft
entries.summary: Chainalysis analyzes the February 21 Bybit theft and its work tracing stolen assets with the exchange and investigators. Treat actor attribution and transaction analysis as the researcher's findings; asset-tracing visibility does not itself establish recovery or the security of a wallet workflow.

entries.title: StepSecurity detects poisoned tj-actions changed-files releases
entries.summary: StepSecurity documents CVE-2025-30066, a compromised GitHub Action that exposed CI secrets through build logs. Its investigation highlights mutable tags and downstream credential exposure. Compare exact workflow revisions and logs rather than assuming every repository using the action lost secrets.

entries.title: Microsoft issues SharePoint guidance for active ToolShell attacks
entries.summary: Microsoft warns of active attacks against on-premises SharePoint and tracks CVE-2025-53770/53771. The revision history separates the July 19 initial notice from later fixes and investigation advice, including machine-key rotation. A patch alone does not establish that prior access was removed.

entries.title: Google tracks OAuth-token theft through Salesloft Drift integrations
entries.summary: GTIG describes stolen OAuth tokens enabling data theft from Salesforce instances linked to Salesloft Drift. Its August 28 update extends guidance to other connected integrations. The campaign illustrates delegated-token risk; it is not a claim that the core Salesforce or Google Workspace platform was compromised.

entries.title: F5 publishes lessons and customer guidance after its security incident
entries.summary: F5 discusses its recently disclosed intrusion and access to BIG-IP source code, while stating that its reviews found no evidence of software supply-chain modification. The follow-up is a first-party assessment, not independent proof of absence or a finding that every customer's device was compromised.

entries.title: CERT-EU warns of WSUS remote code execution
entries.summary: CERT-EU describes CVE-2025-59287, an unauthenticated code-execution flaw affecting Windows Server with the WSUS role enabled. Review the vendor's affected-product and update guidance; a Windows installation alone does not establish applicability.

entries.title: GTIG documents AI-enabled malware and threat-actor tool use
entries.summary: Google reports both experimental and operational AI-enabled malware, including runtime model calls and abuse of developer AI tools. Distinguish observed activity from prototypes; review model-API egress and the privileges held by local AI tooling.

entries.title: Anthropic discloses an AI-orchestrated espionage campaign
entries.summary: Anthropic reports a campaign detected in September 2025 that abused Claude Code against selected organizations. Attribution and automation estimates are the provider's assessments. This November disclosure does not date the start of activity to the history window.

entries.title: GitLab identifies a renewed Shai-Hulud npm campaign
entries.summary: GitLab researchers describe infected npm packages that steal developer and cloud credentials, propagate through publishing access and include destructive behavior. Review dependency histories and credential exposure; package counts in this ongoing report are not a complete victim inventory.

entries.title: React discloses remote code execution in Server Components
entries.summary: The React team discloses CVE-2025-55182 in React Server Components payload decoding. Review affected server packages and the latest vendor patch guidance. Client-only React applications without the relevant server integration are outside the described scope.

entries.title: FBI updates warning on AI-voice impersonation of officials
entries.summary: The FBI updates a continuing campaign, observed since at least 2023, using impersonated officials and AI-generated voice messages to seek codes, documents or payments. Verify requests through a previously trusted channel. December 2025 is this update's date, not the campaign's beginning.

entries.title: Canadian Cyber Centre warns of exploited Ivanti EPMM flaws
entries.summary: The advisory covers CVE-2026-1281 and CVE-2026-1340 in Ivanti EPMM and records vendor-reported exploitation. Its April update adds later KEV context. Review exact versions and vendor analysis guidance; the January publication and subsequent updates remain distinct.

entries.title: ESET analyzes PromptSpy's model-assisted Android persistence
entries.summary: ESET analyzes Android malware that asks Gemini for UI actions supporting persistence and includes remote-access functionality. ESET had not observed PromptSpy in its telemetry and considers a proof of concept possible. This is research evidence, not confirmed widespread deployment.

entries.title: Aqua discloses Trivy release and GitHub Action compromise
entries.summary: Aqua's advisory describes malicious Trivy releases and altered Action tags, followed by compromised container images. Review artifact versions, digests and exposure windows against retained CI evidence; changing a mutable tag alone does not resolve potentially stolen credentials.

entries.title: LiteLLM reports compromised March PyPI releases
entries.summary: LiteLLM identifies malicious PyPI releases 1.82.7 and 1.82.8. Its follow-up describes a compromised CI scanning dependency and release-credential exposure. Match installed artifacts and release windows before applying the vendor's incident-response guidance.

entries.title: US agencies warn of disruptive intrusions into exposed PLCs
entries.source_name: FBI, CISA and US government partners
entries.summary: The joint advisory reports Iran-affiliated activity against internet-facing PLCs, including project-file access and HMI/SCADA manipulation causing disruption. It recommends controlled OT connectivity and vendor-specific hardening. It does not establish exposure of any particular local device.

entries.title: Google studies prompt-injection attempts on the public web
entries.summary: Google's web study distinguishes benign examples from attempts to steer browsing agents toward manipulation, exfiltration or destruction. The study is not exhaustive and observed instructions do not prove successful compromise. Treat retrieved pages as untrusted data in agent workflows.

entries.title: Anthropic reports early Project Glasswing findings
entries.summary: Anthropic describes AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and the remaining verification, disclosure and remediation workload. Aggregate findings include estimates and assessed subsets; they are not evidence that every reported issue is validated or exploited. Plan triage and patch capacity alongside discovery.

entries.title: Oracle issues PeopleSoft PeopleTools security alert
entries.summary: Oracle addresses CVE-2026-35273 in PeopleSoft PeopleTools, describing unauthenticated remote code execution. Check the affected supported versions and mitigation document. The vendor's exploitability description alone is not a finding of compromise in an organization's deployment.

entries.title: Sysdig documents JADEPUFFER agentic database extortion
entries.summary: Sysdig describes an observed agent-driven intrusion involving exposed application infrastructure, credential collection and destructive database extortion. The account is vendor research. Review orchestration-service exposure, secret scope and recoverability rather than assuming an AI label changes the required controls.

entries.title: Hugging Face publishes its evaluation-agent intrusion timeline
entries.summary: Hugging Face reconstructs a July intrusion by an agent running an external model evaluation, including sandbox and infrastructure trust-boundary failures. Review evaluation containment, egress and credential boundaries. This is an incident account, not proof that all AI agents behave this way.

entries.title: Singapore CSA warns of Keyv-related npm compromise
entries.summary: CSA describes malicious Keyv and related npm releases in a self-propagating campaign that steals developer credentials. Compare exact versions and published indicators with retained build records, then follow the advisory's scoped credential and environment response guidance.

entries.title: GTIG reports a shift toward agent-enabled threat operations
entries.summary: Google reports Q2 activity using agent-enabled credential harvesting and targeting AI development assets. Observations span several campaigns, not one September incident. Review cloud identities, AI tooling inputs and secret access, while retaining the report's attribution and telemetry limits.

entries.title: Microsoft tracks passkey-themed cloud identity compromise
entries.summary: Microsoft reports intrusions observed since May using help-desk and passkey pretexts, AiTM or device-code flows, and later cloud data access. The lure is not evidence that passkey cryptography was broken. Correlate sign-ins, authentication-method changes and token activity.

entries.title: Microsoft examines browser patch-gap exploitation
entries.summary: Microsoft describes campaigns exploiting gaps between public Chromium fixes, vendor releases and installed browser updates. Its account suggests AI may accelerate exploit development; this is an assessment, not certainty for every campaign. Update deployment and browser restart both matter.

entries.title: Mandiant investigates short-lived AOMEI update tampering
entries.source_name: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant
entries.summary: Mandiant describes repeated brief changes to AOMEI update infrastructure between April and July 2026, distributing a downloader and backdoor before reverting legitimate configuration. Point-in-time checks may miss such windows; retain update and endpoint telemetry for historical review.

entries.title: LiteLLM publishes corrected October compromise investigation
entries.summary: LiteLLM's canonical investigation explains the October 21 malicious 1.107.0 release through exposed and unrevoked agent-platform credentials and organization-level access. It supersedes parts of the initial account. Distinguish this incident from March and verify exact affected artifacts and response guidance.
